title: Effects of welding sequence and thickness on mechanical response and tensile properties
abstract: This study investigates the effects of welding sequence and plate thickness on the residual stress, residual deformation, and tensile properties of T-joint fillet welds in 5083-H116 aluminum alloy by combining experimental measurements and numerical simulation methods. A series of welding experiments are conducted to explore the molten pool morphology, temperature history curves, residual stress magnitude, residual deformation distribution, and tensile behavior. Thermo-elastic-plastic sequential coupling analysis and tensile fracture behavior analysis of the T-joints are conducted based on the double-ellipsoidal heat source model and the ductile damage model. It is demonstrated that the molten pool, temperature field, residual stress, residual deformation, and tensile properties obtained from experimental measurements are basically consistent with the numerical simulation results. Welding sequence and plate thickness have significant effects on residual stress and residual deformation. The thicker fillet-welded joint fabricated by single-side block welding generates the lowest residual stress in the welding zone. Double-side welding has significant advantages in controlling welding deformation. When subjected to tensile loading, the stress concentration in the weld zone increases considering residual stress compared to the case of ignoring it.
